original_question: Let S be a set, and let T ⊆ S be a subset. Classify those maps f : S → S with the property that for every α ∈ S, the set n ≥ 0 : f n (α) ∈ T has some nice structure, for example, it is the union of finitely many one-sided arithmetic progressions.
target_in_paper: Question 2.3 in Section 2, made precise in Section 7 as Conjecture 7.1 (the Dynamical Mordell-Lang Conjecture).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the core return-time set {n >= 0 : f^n(alpha) in T} and the intended structural conclusion that this set should be a finite union of one-sided arithmetic progressions. That is essentially the abstract template stated in Question 2.3, and it points to the paper's precise algebraic-dynamical version in Conjecture 7.1.
missing_details: The paper's precise setting is not an arbitrary set S, but a quasi-projective variety X over C.
The subset T is not arbitrary; it is a subvariety Y subseteq X.
The map f is not an arbitrary self-map of a set; it is a morphism f : X -> X.
The official conjecture quantifies over every point P in X and every subvariety Y subseteq X.
The notation f^n should be specified as the n-th iterate of f, with n >= 0.
The paper defines a one-sided arithmetic progression in N to mean a set of the form {a k + b : k = 0,1,2,...} with integers a,b >= 0, and it explicitly allows a = 0, so singleton sets are included.
The precise paper-faithful formulation is a conjecture asserting the arithmetic-progression conclusion in this algebraic setting, not a general classification problem for arbitrary set maps.
The nearby discussion starts with wandering points as motivation, but wandering is not a hypothesis in the formal statement of Conjecture 7.1.
The geometric significance of an infinite intersection is explained via periodic/preperiodic subvarieties in Definition 7.2; that context is absent from the draft.
refined_question: Let X/C be a quasi-projective variety, let f : X -> X be a morphism, let P be a point of X, and let Y subseteq X be a subvariety. Writing f^n for the n-th iterate of f, is the set {n >= 0 : f^n(P) in Y} always a finite union of one-sided arithmetic progressions {a k + b : k = 0,1,2,...} with integers a,b >= 0 (allowing a = 0, so singletons are permitted)?
justification: The draft is almost verbatim the abstract meta-question in Question 2.3, but the paper's exact research-level formulation of that idea is Conjecture 7.1 in Section 7. Section 7 specializes the abstract set-theoretic language to arithmetic dynamics on quasi-projective varieties over C, defines precisely what counts as a one-sided arithmetic progression, and states the conjecture in that setting. The nearby Definition 7.2 explains the periodic/preperiodic subvariety obstruction behind infinite intersections, Theorem 7.3 records important proved cases, and Remark 7.7 identifies the conjecture as the dynamical analogue of classical Mordell-Lang.
